ParlaMint-AT_2007-01-16-023-XXIII-NRSITZ-00009_d7e4455	Mr President of the Federal Republic of Germany! Madam President of the National Council! High house! My venerations Ladies and gentlemen! Whatever we politicians do, whatever we want to do in the next four years, we focus on Austria and the well-being of the Austrians. [[Congratulations with SPÖ and ÖVP.]] For this reason, it is a great honour to be able to present to you today as the Federal Chancellor the programme of the new Federal Government in its basic features. But before I go into the plans for the future, allow me to look back briefly. ==References== In October 2006, the voters in our country made their decision. The outcome of the National Council elections has made Austrian Social Democracy the strongest and strongest political group in Parliament, followed by the Austrian People's Party. My aim was to fulfil the mandate of the President of the Federal Government to form a new federal government in such a way as to achieve the most stable government possible for this legislative period. I therefore invited the chairman of the second strongest party, Dr Wolfgang Schüssel, to negotiate. All of you, ladies and gentlemen, know the course of these negotiations, which were very difficult in stages. On both sides not always had great confidence. Deeply there and there may also have been injuries and reservations arising from the conflicts between government and opposition in recent years. Finally, two parties have also negotiated with each other, which in many respects have different views and programmes. I say this very openly here and today because these differences will not suddenly have disappeared. In view of the outcome of the elections, euphoria may also have contributed to irritation on the one hand and disappointment on the other. These have now been cleared out. Instead, the awareness that the willingness to compromise and cooperate is one of the essences of democracy has become a common joy and confidence to lead our country into a good future in the years to come. Finally, both negotiators have also been aware of their responsibility to the Sovereign, to the citizens of our country. The election result was a task for cooperation if you want to have a stable federal government. And so we have agreed a cooperation between the S & D Party and the Austrian People's Party for the next four years – with a very ambitious program that carries the manuscript of both partners. Another open word: Major coalitions are under a certain general suspicion. The interplay between government and opposition would be eliminated by a too large parliamentary majority, pro-poor and post-checkers would be on the agenda, and some other accusations could be listed more. But let's think back. We note that there have been times when great coalitions have actually done great things – such as the reconstruction of our country after the disaster of National Socialism or the accession of Austria to the European Union. On the other hand, we can also remember periods of standstill and blockade. Large coalitions are neither good nor bad in themselves. It is about what the two partners do, how they deal with each other, how open they are to opposition proposals and initiatives or from outside Parliament. In short, it is about whether the dangers are being hit or the chances of such cooperation being used. We are faced with this challenge, ladies and gentlemen, of which I am aware, of which my colleagues in the Federal Government are aware – and this will ultimately also be the performance of this federal government. And tasks await us to a sufficient extent. The responsibility is great. I would like to outline the fundamental objectives of the new Federal Government before I want to deal with individual issues. I am based on the wishes and concerns of people in our country. What do the Austrians expect from politics today? They expect – this shows all personal encounters and conversations – no wonder things, they have a very realistic picture of what politics is capable of doing. People in Austria want to have opportunities to develop, to stand on their own feet and to live their lives the way they imagine it. They want to be well prepared for the future. They want fair conditions, a fair balance of rights and obligations, they want performance to be rewarded. And they want so much social warmth and security that they can live in dignity, even if they suffer a fate. They don't want to be afraid of old age, and they want their children and grandchildren to be good, even better than themselves. We live in a good and also in a relatively rich country. Nevertheless, few people have the impression that they are not so good, or are concerned that their children will once be worse than themselves. Many of these fears focus on globalisation or seemingly unchangeable developments. Undoubtedly: International conditions, whether the international economy or the development of the global climate, can only be limited by politics here in Austria. In politics, on the other hand, we should not act as if there were no more spaces of design at all, as if we had always had to give up on matters from the outside without any contradictions. No, the task of politics is to create as many opportunities for people as possible for the future and to give protection and security wherever possible. Individual performance needs to be promoted, while at the same time a social climate of security, mutual respect and interaction needs to be fostered in dignity. It is part of our task to ensure greater cohesion in our society. [[Congratulations with SPÖ and ÖVP.]] This basic attitude, this balance shape this federal government, and it is also guided by the plans of the new government. We will stimulate economic growth and combat unemployment, increase the competitiveness of the economy of our country and pursue a sound budgetary policy, develop and financially secure our social and health systems, increase poverty reduction, improve opportunities for both citizens and businesses with offensive education and research policies, strengthen women's opportunities in our society and take great steps towards gender equality, promote open and living art and cultural life, maintain high quality of life and the environment in our country, ensure the highest possible level of internal and external security to protect people, strengthen democracy and fundamental rights with a state and administrative reform, and strengthen the country's internal structure for the requirements of the 21st century. In the century, and actively and comprehensively in the European Union, and in general strengthen international cooperation and work for peace in the world as a top priority. Work, ladies and gentlemen, is out of our common conviction the best condition for a self-determined, self-responsible life. That is why we want to significantly reduce unemployment, at least by a quarter and thus by less than 4 per cent until the end of this legislative period. I know that's an ambitious goal, and some think, an unattainable one. But I'm fully convinced: It is to be done and we will also achieve it! [[Congratulations with the SPÖ and representatives of the ÖVP.]] To this end, we are relying on intensive programmes to promote economic growth. Special priorities will be the further increase in the promotion of research and development, as well as significant investments in infrastructure. It is particularly important to us that the young people in Austria are not on the road. With an educational guarantee up to the age of 18, we want to drastically reduce the proportion of young people without vocational training or schooling, increase employment opportunities accordingly, and thus fight youth unemployment in a sustainable way. With the maintenance of special resources for active labour market policies and a national action programme for older workers, we will reduce unemployment. We will also intensify the fight against black entrepreneurship and black work, for example through increased control and higher sanctions. However, we also want to improve the quality of jobs and establish a single modern worker concept. The growing number of atypical workers will be better safeguarded socially. The Federal Government is committed to a social and ecologically sustainable market economy in fair competition. The development and improvement of the international competitiveness of the economic location within the framework of the European Partnership for Growth and Employment is a declared objective. A special focus will be placed on the Federal Government with special measures in favour of small and medium-sized enterprises. We want to ensure that favourable capital is provided for necessary investments, that business transfers are made legally easier and tax-promoting and that business start-ups are also fully supported. Social security for self-employed people will be improved. A protected “master company” seal is to be introduced as guidance for consumers. For the creation of businesses, more competition in the field of professions is intended to reduce the cost of founding and we want to review the establishment of a stability fund to provide risk capital to young innovative companies. The Internationalisation Plan is also being continued in view of the importance of the export economy for the success of the Austrian economy. In addition, there are a number of other projects, such as the more flexible granting of employment permits for professionals from the new EU countries in sectors with special needs and a socially compatible flexibility of working time. In the field of research, innovation and technology, the new Federal Government is committed to making both a qualitative and quantitative leap forward. In order to ensure growth and employment in Austria, the research rate must be increased and structural change forced: In the next few years, Austria will increasingly become an independent producer of top technology and a top-ranking research location that we can be proud of. By 2010 the research rate will be increased to 3 percent by gradually increasing the existing budgets by a total of € 800 million. This will also trigger as much private research investment as possible. At the same time, the large number of support programmes must be adjusted and more efficient. But the most important resource in the field of research and innovation – human beings – is to be particularly promoted. The creation of new posts for researchers, their mobility from and to Austria, as well as between sectors, as well as the increase in the share of women in both the public and private research sectors are particularly important. The planned technology leadership requires both excellent public research structures and entrepreneurial research. This extends from the reform of the Academy of Sciences to measures for small and medium-sized enterprises with research activities to a headquarters strategy for research and development. A modern infrastructure policy is essential for the success of the economic location and thus for the creation of new jobs. We want to achieve the optimization of the Austrian transport system through a meaningful link between the various modes of transport. Rail and waterways should become more attractive in terms of environmental compatibility as transport routes. The priority in road and rail infrastructure is to close gaps and eliminate bottlenecks in the high-level network. To implement the ÖBB Framework Plan, we will invest €6 billion in this legislative period, and another €4.5 billion in the ASFINAG construction programme. [[Congratulations with the SPÖ and representatives of the ÖVP.]] Public transport is crucial especially in centres for the mobility of people and economic development. In rural regions, it serves public health and social justice. We will make the offer of public transport more attractive. Investment in public transport is not least an important contribution to reducing the burden of greenhouse gas, fine dust and nitrogen oxide. Austria's airline location is also to be further developed, including through quality offensives at airports as well as better networking with road and rail. Transport safety is a high priority for the new Federal Government. That is why we want to achieve improvements in control systems, speed limits, heavy traffic controls and driving training. In transit, there will be a new strategy for greater cost-effectiveness in freight transport. The truck toll is revised, differentiated and increased. Ladies and gentlemen! I come to budget and financial policy. In my view, ordered state finances are not self-evident, but they are an extremely important condition for policy to be and remain operational. If major initiatives are to be put in place for our country or if a weak economic economy needs to be countered, then we need the corresponding resources in the government budget. That is why I stand for a stable budget and for responsible and economical handling of taxpayers' money! The Federal Government is therefore committed to a sound and sustainable budgetary and financial policy that balances over a cycle of economics. This goal requires discipline. The scope for tax relief is to be developed and, in the light of the background, it is necessary to ensure that important future investments for growth and employment, the location of Austria, social security or other important public tasks are also made. The Federal Government pays attention to the common budgetary responsibility of all local authorities within the meaning of the Austrian Stability Pact. In this legislative period, the Federal Government will implement a major tax reform with a tangible discharge of taxpayers and the economy. [[Congratulations with SPÖ and ÖVP.]] The tax and tax system should be sustainable. Ecological aspects are included and a positive economic development is supported. We want to ensure the best possible climate and a functioning and fair capital market. We will work, among other things, at European level, to harmonise the relevant standards, to strengthen market and abuse supervision and to strengthen transparency rules. Ladies and gentlemen! A key task of this federal government is the further development of our overall proven system of social security and fairness. This development must never stop, the challenges, the divisions in our society and the injustices are changing too quickly. If we want to have an activated and modern social state, it must meet the current requirements, and it must be operational, that is, funded securely. Under these conditions, we can achieve greater justice, security and also greater willingness to innovation and initiative. [[Congratulations with the SPÖ and representatives of the ÖVP.]] Pensions are the most essential prerequisites for enabling the older generation to live in dignity. We agreed that no pensioner, no pensioner, must live below the poverty line. The compensatory allowance rate – that is, our kind of minimum pension – is raised to € 726. We are therefore among the top three countries in the European Union! Financial page 163 Preamble The S & D Party of Austria and the Austrian People's Party conclude this Convention with the aim of establishing a joint federal government on the basis of the content of this Convention for the XXIII. This is the first time we have been able to find a solution to this problem. The aim is to build up and further improve citizens on the basis of what has been achieved so far. Further offensives for the growth of the economy with the aim of full employment by 2010 require additional measures to combat unemployment and the competitiveness of the economic location in international comparison and the continuation of a solid budgetary policy with a view to achieving a balanced budget over the economic cycle. Another focus will be the further development of the Austrian social and health system, which will be complemented by a poverty reduction strategy. An offensive education and research policy is a prerequisite for addressing international competition challenges. The promotion of an open and living art and cultural life will be particularly important for the Federal Government. The high quality of life and the environment in Austria is to be maintained. The focus of government work is on the highest possible level of internal and external security to protect citizens. By means of a state and administrative reform, the internal structure of the Republic in the Federal Republic of Germany, countries and municipalities is also intended to meet the new requirements of the 21st century. ==References====External links== The continued fidelity of the Republic of Austria ("PACTa sunt servanda") is beyond dispute. Therefore, international agreements, European commitments, applications and contracts – whether they be state-of-the-art or private administration – are not disputed. The participation of Austria in the European Union is intended to serve the interests of our country, its citizens, and to contribute to the success of the European integration process. Austria will actively participate in the further development of the Union, through full participation in the integration in political, economic, social and foreign policy and security matters. In relations with other States and through cooperation in international organisations, such as the United Nations, the Austrian Government aims to achieve the highest level of international cooperation and to maintain peace as a top priority. Parliamentary procedure In principle, on the basis of the government programme, the two government parties will jointly represent their concerns in government and Parliament. Government documents are dealt with and decided quickly in Parliament; when drawing up the timetable, a sufficient period of time should be provided for the assessment and coordination with the countries and for thorough parliamentary consultation with the opposition parties. In addition to joint parliamentary initiatives, each government party can set up its own legislative legislative initiatives. Prior to this, they must be communicated to the other government partner as far as possible a week before and to negotiate with him with a view to a joint contribution. Each Government Party shall approve applications for parliamentary surveys and inquiry committees proposed by the Government Party, after previous negotiations, at the latest in the second Committee meeting following the submission. The two government parties are seeking dialogue with all parties represented in Parliament on the basis of the government programme. This also includes discussing their proposals in a factual and constructive manner and, if agreed, taking a decision. Reports of the Federal Government shall be discussed in plenary in accordance with a key to be agreed with the opposition parties. All parliamentary decisions, including those on Rules of Procedure, must be taken in a timely manner by the two club members in order to achieve a joint decision-making process. Examining committees are obliged to do their job. Austria – Partners in Europe and the world 1. For a strong, social and modern Europe Europe must benefit and protect citizens. The Federal Government is therefore committed to a strong, united Europe. These include: deepening the community of values and strengthening the European model of life with its distinct social dimension: preserving and respecting European diversity, balancing social security, economic dynamics and sustainability; the extension of the common market Europe's foreign and security policy and solidarity contributions to common EU missions; more Europe in the field of security, justice and home affairs. More European cooperation in the field of migration (recovery agreements, data exchange) and a fair distribution of responsibility in the reception and care of asylum seekers; improved cross-border police cooperation; in the field of energy, enhanced coordination among European partners. Europe needs more security of supply through diversification of energy resources, the development of renewable energy sources and the strictest safety standards in nuclear energy. The Federal Government will work towards new initiatives in the field of sustainable energy policy, in particular with a view to substantially reducing Europe's dependence on nuclear energy; the closure of remaining gaps in the European internal market. Strengthening the confidence of Austrians in the European project is a particular concern of the Federal Government. To this end, it will be increasingly seeking new ways of mediation. The aim is to revitalise citizens' awareness of Europe, thus greatly strengthening the acceptance of the European integration work in Austria. Foreign and European policies are inseparably interwoven, so the distribution of competences between the Federal Chancellery and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs will not be altered. The aim is to guarantee the optimum enforcement of Austrian interests through the greatest possible coherence and efficiency. 2. Reunification of Europe The Federal Government is committed to the peace project Europe. Relations with all neighbouring countries are as close and close as ever before. The Federal Government is committed to strengthening targeted cooperation with neighbouring countries. We will have an active neighbourhood policy both bilaterally and within the EU in the format of the “Regional Partnership” (in addition to Austria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia) as well as in the context of the issues of the Western Balkans. The Federal Government will ensure that the enlargement process takes full account of the EU's capacity to accept it carefully and prudently. European integration is incomplete without the countries of the Western Balkans. They all have an accession perspective: In line with the needs of the domestic labour market, the accession agreements with the States acceding in May 2004 and the conditions and protective measures provided for in Bulgaria and Romania; With the accession of Bulgaria and Romania, the Danube will essentially become an inflow of the European Union. The potential of this river, not only as a transport arteries, but also in the areas of culture, the environment and tourism, is to be revived in a comprehensive way; The EU accession negotiations with Croatia will be continued with determination and concluded as early as possible; A targeted and careful approach to European values and standards for Turkey and its people is in the interests of all Member States of the European Union. Austria has insisted that negotiations with Turkey have an open outcome. We are committed to a step-by-step approach with the aim of a tailor-made Turkish-European Community. In any case, the Austrian citizens will have the last word in a referendum with a goal of accession in a referendum. With the help of the EU's European Neighbourhood Policy, the neighbouring countries of the Union, Ukraine and Moldova should be brought to the fullest possible conclusions on European values and standards. Particular attention should be paid to the special importance of relations between the European Union and Russia. An active and open policy must be pursued towards those countries on our continent which are in a specific close relationship with the European Union, such as Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Iceland. 3rd. Reform of EU institutions We will continue to play an active and equal role in the future of the European peace project in all policy areas. The Federal Government considers the Constitutional Treaty approved by the National Council in 2005 to be a balanced and further basis in order to ensure Europe's ability to act in the future. We will play an active part in this constructive discussion. In any case, the Federal Government is committed to a “Europe of concrete projects” as well as to a more efficient and Make more transparent use of the existing Treaties in order to bring EU policies closer to citizens. The EU should only carry out those tasks which can really be done better in Brussels in the Community, as well as more involve national representatives (subsidiarity). 4. Economic and monetary union The creation of a suitable framework for more jobs, growth and social security is the central concern of the Federal Government. It will therefore firmly implement the newly-oriented Lisbon Strategy for growth and employment. This applies in particular to the concrete targets agreed under the Austrian Presidency on youth employment, business start-ups and the promotion of SMEs. (e.g. by 2010 annual creation of at least 2 million additional jobs; by the end of 2007, each unemployed school leaver is expected to work within 6 months. a job, apprenticeship, further training or any other job-preparing measure is offered; by 2010 achieving 3% research rate; by 2007 ‘one-stop-shops’ for business start-ups.) The Federal Government will work to create common EU minimum standards in the fields of employment and social affairs. The Federal Government will take action to strengthen coordination between the EU, the EU Member States and the social partners at European level in the interests of reducing high levels of unemployment. Innovation and research are important factors for EU competitiveness. The Federal Government therefore supports the creation of a European Institute of Technology (EIT) as a network for the promotion of excellence in research, education and innovation. It offers Austria as the seat of the EIT Secretariat and is willing to make an appropriate contribution to financing and infrastructure. A wide-ranging review of the EU financial system is planned for the coming years: The Federal Government is committed to responsible handling of European taxpayers and therefore to a economical EU budget, to optimising the return to Austria and a long-term solution to the EU's own resources issue. In this context, the Federal Government will focus on particular areas of rural development and development. Promoting sustainable projects (research and development). No ‘funding euro’ may be left to lie in Brussels. Austria will continue to take a leading position in rural development. The Federal Government will continue its consolidation policy in full compliance with the EU reformed Stability and Growth Pact. It will pay particular attention to the reduction of the general government deficit and a sustainable reduction in the debt ratio under the Maastricht criteria. The Federal Government will continue its previous initiatives within the framework of the European institutions to ensure the feasibility of this on a minimum basis. an EU-wide tax such as: Review a foreign exchange transaction tax and work towards uniform implementation steps, without endangering the Lisbon objectives. Liquefied financial resources will be allocated to an EU fund that balances the allocation of supranational tasks such as EU own funding and development cooperation. 5. External security The Federal Government is committed to a comprehensive peace policy. On the basis of its constitutionally defined ever-increasing neutrality, Austria will continue to be a reliable and solid partner in the world and actively participate in the further development of European security and defence policy. This includes the achievement of the existing EU planning target (headline goal 2010), with particular reference to ensuring the rapid response capacity of the EU. At the same time, EU civil crisis management instruments should be expanded, taking into account the EU 2008 planning targets. A focus of the Austrian foreign and security policy commitment will continue to remain the West Balkan. Stability in this region means security for Europe and Austria. Austria's foreign policy, particularly within the framework of the EU, will continue to work hard for a peace solution in the Middle East on the basis of Road Map. It will actively use its good relations with all the countries of the region, including Israel. A priority will be the continuation and expansion of aid to Palestinians and dialogue with Arab civil society. In general, our relationship with the Islamic world requires special attention. Building on the many positive impulses in international relations for Austria during its EU Presidency, relations with Latin America, Asia and Africa should be strengthened. The Federal Government will work towards a deeper transatlantic partnership in the bilateral relations of Austria with the USA and Canada and within the framework of the EU, based on the common values of democracy and the rule of law. 6. United Nations and multilateral questions The United Nations is the core competence centre for the international promotion of peace, security and justice. Austria is committed to the principle of effective multilateralism and will continue to contribute actively to the work of the United Nations, in particular in the areas of peacekeeping, protection of human rights, disarmament, protection of the environment, equality of women and the fight against terrorism, organised crime and drug trafficking. The focus of our initiatives is on: Austria's candidate for a non-resident seat in the UN Security Council in the years 2009-2010; increased financial support, in particular through a sustainable increase in voluntary contributions, by 2008 at the latest; strengthening Austria as the headquarters of international organisations and conferences. Vienna is a global centre of competence for international security and energy of the UN and OSCE; the traditional good dialogue within Austria of groups of different religious beliefs. It will host Austria as a host of conferences on the dialogue of cultures and To strengthen religions and to be a model for European dialogue to improve peaceful co-existence. The inclusion of European Islam in this dialogue takes a special position; Women's policy in development cooperation and peace work. In the case of international efforts to rebuild societies in post-conflict situations, the position of women is to be strengthened – as vulnerable people in the countries as well as as as decision-makers in the missions. Additional appropriations are the subject of the budget negotiations. The Federal Government will continue its active efforts for disarmament and arms control, as well as for the spread of nuclear weapons and for the further development of international humanitarian law. The Federal Government is actively committed to respect for human rights at European level and worldwide. It promotes the transformation of the EU Racism Observatory in Vienna into an EU Human Rights Agency with the broadest possible mandate. The Federal Government will be committed to further strengthening the OSCE, taking particular account of the areas of democracy development, human rights protection and election observation. 7. Development cooperation and foreign culture policy Development cooperation (ECA) and foreign culture are integral elements of foreign policy. The Federal Government acknowledges the decisions of the EU Council, according to which a share of 0.51% of the gross national income is to be used for EZA services by 2010. It will also focus on cluster education in the fields of medicine, technology for small and medium-sized enterprises, education and energy. In the context of the international disaster aid, the people concerned continue to provide rapid and efficient solidarity aid. The main concern of development cooperation is to win women as partners and to promote them. Each specific project of development cooperation will be examined to see whether it takes account of women’s concerns and particular interests. The Federal Government will work to strengthen coherence in development policy in all its areas of activity and to further evaluate the activities of the Austrian Development Agency (ADA) and the coordination mechanism. A positive economic upturn can lead the poorest countries in the world out of poverty. It is therefore necessary to broaden the efforts undertaken in the framework of "Economic Development". In addition to the United Nations, the World Bank, the OECD Development Assistance Committee, the EU and most donor countries, the Austrian EZA is also committed to winning Austrian companies to participate in the achievement of the UN Millennium Goals. The Austrian Federal Government is committed to strengthening the placement of a comprehensive Austrian image abroad to support Austrian interests. The network of cultural forums and Austrian libraries can be used as a successful platform and engine for the authentic, target group-oriented presentation of modern Austria. The Federal Government supports Linz as the European Capital of Culture 2009 (together with Vilnius). This nomination gives the state capital and the whole Region new impetus and the opportunity to present itself as a creative and forward-looking cultural region with a sustainable impact. 8. Offensive “citizen service” The Ministry of Foreign Affairs should be further expanded as a service: Adjusting the foreign network to meet foreign policy, economic and consular requirements in order to best represent the interests of Austrians abroad. The Federal Government will work to ensure that, in addition to fulfilling its obligations in the design of Austrian foreign policy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs can also fulfil its role as a modern service company for citizens, business and politics, and will take the necessary human resources to do so. Austrian foreign policy will continue to support Austrian companies, in close cooperation with the Economic Chamber, in their efforts to successfully anchor themselves in the domestic and international markets. A particular focus will be placed on the perception of Austrian interests within the framework of international trade policy. Improved crisis and disaster management: The aim is to ensure local consular care for the emergency where thousands of Austrian tourists live each year. Human reinforcements in the consular and civil service sectors in Germany and abroad, as well as improved networking at bi-multi-teral level, should therefore be ensured. Additional appropriations are the subject of the budget negotiations. Information campaigns on foreign and EU policy issues (e.g. also on the homepage of the BMAA, target group-oriented). The Federal Government is committed to a secure and non-useful visa system: In order to ensure a safe, thorough and efficient processing and control of constantly increasing numbers of visa applications, sufficient specialist personnel and modern devices to detect fake documents must be ensured. In order to optimise the use of resources, together with EU partners, the establishment of joint visa offices will also be carried out. Biometry Center Tested. External security and defence We live in a stabilised Europe that is not exposed to a conventional threat. This is a solid foundation for the peaceful development of our continent. The Federal Government is committed to a comprehensive peace policy. On the basis of its constitutionally defined ever-increasing neutrality, Austria will continue to be a reliable and solid partner in the world and actively participate in the further development of European security and defence policy. Austria has been valued internationally as a place of meeting and dialogue and has proven this during the EU Presidency 2006. Many international organisations such as the UN, the OSCE and the Organization of Earth Exporting Countries (OPEC) are based in Austria. The Federal Government wants to strengthen Austria and, in particular, Vienna as the seat of important organisations. The achievement of solidarity within the EU is part of the Austrian peace policy. Austria will therefore actively participate in the further development of European Security and Defence Policy (ESDP). One priority is the achievement of the existing EU planning target (headline goal 2010), taking into account in particular the security of the EU's rapid response capacity. At the same time, EU civil crisis management instruments should be expanded, taking into account the EU 2008 planning targets. In this context, the Federal Government will ensure that the necessary organisational, legal and budgetary arrangements are made to ensure the rapid deployment of Austrian experts from the police and judicial sectors, civil administration and relevant non-governmental organisations for civilian crisis management. Missions should be optimised in accordance with the Court of Auditors’ proposals (BUND series, 2006/11), regardless of whether they concern military or civil forces. The EU can contribute very significantly to stability and security in crisis regions through its common foreign and security policy. Wars or conflicts rob people of their future prospects, increased immigration pressure trigger refugee flows and strengthen the activities of criminal organizations. It is therefore important that the EU – and in its context also Austria – actively contribute to ensuring peace and international stability, as is already done in different forms and with different instruments, especially in the Balkans, but also in the Middle East and Africa. In order to stabilise international crises, military presence will continue to be necessary in the future. With its peace efforts, but also in dealing with natural disasters in Germany and abroad, the Austrian Federal Army is doing particularly valuable work. Austria has so far participated above average in unled peace missions in international comparison and will continue this tradition. Moreover, Austria will continue to participate actively in PfP activities in close cooperation with the other non-neutral and alliance-free participating countries of the Partnership for Peace (PfP). The Federal Government guarantees the ability of the Austrian Federal Government to act. A federal army is necessary to carry out its tasks in the field of military defence and to protect sovereignty and neutrality. The German army must effectively assist the population in the event of disaster and enable the best possible protection of the population from nuclear, biological or chemical threats. The German army must continue to be able to provide its internationally respected services abroad for the security of peace and stability. The Federal Army needs sufficient human resources, but also that organization, equipment, equipment and training for modern armies to meet the requirements of the 21st century. ==References====External links==* Official website The militia will continue to be an integral part of the Federal Army's operational organisation. State and administrative reform On the basis of the work of the Austrian Convention and the Special Committee on this matter, a Constitutional Reform will be prepared, in particular, a modern fundamental rights reform, in particular fundamental social rights, a reorganisation of competences, the strengthening of legal protection and democratic controls, improvements in electoral law, strengthening the country autonomy and the legal status of the municipalities, including constitutional bases for administrative reform and, last but not least, a constitutional adjustment. In order to formulate the necessary legal texts, an expert group is set up at the Federal Chancellor's Office, which is owned by the SPÖ Dr. Kostelka and Dr. Öhlinger, by the ÖVP Dr. Fierce and Dr. Khol as well as two representatives of the national conference. It has its proposals until 30. Reimbursement of June 2007 on the basis of which Parliament's deliberations are to be held with a view to adopting the Constitutional Reform by the end of 2007. 1. Fundamental rights reform The aim is to create a uniform, clear catalogue of fundamental rights in which the currently fragmented fundamental rights guarantees are merged and developed in accordance with the fundamental law catalogue of the Europe Treaty. Fundamental rights should be defined as real guarantees, not as mere declarations. The aim of fundamental rights is to safeguard the freedom of individuals and human dignity. The guarantee of human dignity should therefore be expressly included in the catalogue of fundamental rights. In particular, guarantees against discrimination on grounds of sex, race, social or ethnic origin, disability or other grounds (e.g. Age, sexual orientation) and children's rights to implement the Child Law Convention. In the fundamental rights catalogue, social fundamental rights must be anchored in accordance with the consultations in the Convention. Social policy must in principle be made by means of legislation. Social fundamental rights require a special legal protection system adapted to their nature. At the same time, it should be pointed out that social fundamental rights do not dissuade individuals from their fundamental responsibility for the design of their lives and that the granting of state benefits depends on the economic performance of the community. The establishment of legal professional representations with self-government should be provided for in the Constitution. An appropriate legal protection mechanism is to be provided for enforcement of social fundamental rights as well, based on the proposals in the Austrian Convention, which also provides for the complete absence of a legal regime in the event of a constitutional illegality. 2. New division of tasks between the Federal Government and the Länder The competences of the federal and state states must be re-designed according to a three-pillar model, divided in the sense of two separate areas of competence of the federal and state (first and second pillars) and an area of “common legislation” (third pillar). Further formulations will be made on the basis of the proposals in the Austrian Convention by 30. ==References====External links==* Official website On this basis, negotiations between the Federal Government and countries should be conducted with a view to adopting the constitutional changes by the end of 2007 so that they can find their way into the deliberations of the next financial compensation. Establishment of national administrative courts In particular, the well-developed Austrian legal protection system will be improved significantly by introducing a multi-stage administrative jurisdiction in the sense of a procedural acceleration, an enhanced civil service and the discharge of the administrative court. To this end, administrative courts are set up which are to be composed of a national administrative court per country and an administrative court of the first instance at the federal level for the direct federal administration (the indirect federal administration control the national administration courts). In addition to the “general” national or federal administration court, the creation of further special courts should be permitted. In particular, a special court is to be set up to set up its own federal court, which decides at the last instance. The numerous judicial-like special authorities (e.g. the independent management Senate and the independent financial Senate or the various collegial authorities with judicial intervention) should be transferred as far as possible to the newly created administrative court of first instance; Establishment of own Senates with lay members in the administrative courts for certain areas (at least construction, procurement and service law). In principle, the administrative first instance is to have a reformatory decision-making power, but according to the example of § 66(2) of the AVG, it is also intended to have the possibility of cassatory decision-making. The administrative courts' decisions are to be appealed first to the Administrative Court; the admissibility of the appeal must be determined by the revision model by the administrative court of first instance, with the admissibility decision being the subject of a appeal. According to the Administrative Court, due to the alleged infringement of constitutionally guaranteed rights or the application of an unlawful general standard of the Constitutional Court, which receives a general right of refusal. The members of the currently existing judicial-like special authorities, which are transferred to the new administrative courts, should not automatically become members of the new administrative courts; the acquisition should take place in individual cases in accordance with a rule of law. As this construction gives discharge to the Federal Administrative Court, it is necessary to clarify the financing with the countries. 5. Right to vote During the next legislative period, the active electoral age will be reduced to 16 years. The electoral process abroad is simplified: The absence of the need for the signature of a witness (instead of the voter’s ‘own declaration’), the establishment of foreign-Austrian electoral evidence to the representative authorities, the removal from the local electorate evidence only with the consent of the person concerned. The legislative period will be extended to five years from the next legislative period. Constitutional adjustment Together with the first major constitutional innovations, a constitutional adjustment should be made on the basis of the proposals of the Committee 2 of the Austrian Convention and in accordance with the preparatory work of the working group set up to that end. In addition to the agreement of the parties in the Special Committee on State Borders and State Contracts, this constitutional adjustment is intended to constitute a general arrangement for non-profit-making authorities. In the future, state agreements, which are entitled to self-change, will be able to be adopted without a constitutional change. However, the National Council and the Federal Council are to be granted a right of reservation. The Federal Constitution provides for a general authorisation of the simple legislator for the exemption of public authorities. This authorisation lays down the minimum requirements for such authorities as to protect against their decisions, political responsibility for their decisions and parliamentary control rights. The stock of the legal protection bodies already established is secured by constitutional law. The representation of the Federal Ministers is simplified in agreement with the Presidency Office. The inclusion of a catalogue of basic principles and principles (state objectives) at the beginning of the Constitution should be sought (in particular social and liberal rule of law, peace policy, nuclear freedom, conservation of the water and forest). A further objective of the constitutional reform in this legislative period will be the creation of a “relative inclusion” bid, which will be comprehensive integration of all constitutional laws and constitutional provisions requires. For this purpose, the following principles shall apply: All essential provisions are to be merged into the main instrument of the Constitution. In addition, it is only the one express in the Constitution itself provide a ‘constitutional charter’ as well as a temporary Constitutional Accompanying Act. As constitutional stratators, historically significant constitutional laws are to remain part of the federal constitution. The Constitutional Accompaniment Act is intended to contain transitional provisions as well as temporary provisions, but it is also temporary. The numerous scattered constitutional provisions are to be incorporated or removed as constitutional law. Constitutional changes will be possible in the future only by changing the standard instrument of the Constitution. Constitutional rank with the exception of the Constitutional Strabants. The more detailed design of politically sensitive areas of substantive constitutional law, whose principles are determined only in the federal constitution, is to be carried out by “constitutional federal laws” which themselves are not formal constitutional law but are subject to an increased ("two-thirds legislation"). In order to improve citizens' access to justice, it is necessary to examine whether the legal information system of the Federal Government can be designed as an authentic legal source after a revision in the sense of a “permanent re-announcement”. The group of experts mentioned at the outset discussed the questions of a preamble and a change in the principle of legality. Economy/Location/Work Economic policy The Federal Government is committed to a social and ecologically sustainable market economy with fair competition. The Federal Government supports the future development of the market economy. Under fair, regulated conditions, accompanied by best-trained people, excellent infrastructure, functioning communities, ongoing renewal of social systems and social security of individuals, fair participation of all people in the development of gross domestic product with a view to increasing mass purchasing power, strengthening education including lifelong learning, the ongoing development of science, research and development, better working conditions and fair competition in the sense of a socially fair and innovative competitive economy. In addition, ensuring a comprehensive supply of affordable and high-quality services is ensured by the principle of universal services (e.g. in the field of telecommunications). The further development and improvement of the international competitiveness of the economic and labour location within the framework of the European Partnership for Growth and Employment – Lisbon Process – is a declared objective. Growth and economic policy An efficient growth and economic policy requires a balanced mix of expenditure-side and fiscal measures in the interests of greater growth and employment, with the Federal Government in particular seeking to set out the following measures and objectives: developing and modernising infrastructure; Infrastructural investment programme (rail, road, energy supply, communications networks), an old house restructuring programme with a focus on energy saving, an energy infrastructure development programme including the development of environmentally friendly energy and the use of energy saving facilities, Facilitating the application of PPP models by adapting relevant provisions for tenders; Release of the factor of work improving education and training; creation of a globally competitive innovation environment (research and development, education); raising the R & D ratio to 3% of GDP in the short term by 2010, and improving the quality of research and development policies by focusing on clustering between economy and science, strengthening active labour market policies, The Austrian industry, for example, plays a role in the development of the site. SMEs as subcontractors have a key role to play in this respect; leading competence units and the headquarters (headquarters policy) of Austria must be taken into account in economic and location policies, as well as in the continuing growing services sector. Specific measures for SMEs; reducing restrictions on competition, such as access to professions, and improving regulation to promote effective competition, innovative, cooperative and high-quality public administration; enhancing the efficiency of public administration; implementing a standard cost model, recovery and support of the Austrian capital market, an active foreign trade policy to support an export offensive; Support for Austrian companies in their internationalisation, particularly in the area of expansion through market development, acquisition of foreign companies and investments in Central and Eastern Europe Support for projects of Austrian companies in third world countries by means of development assistance measures; Focus-oriented business-settlement policy and promotion of direct investment; the best possible consideration of the interests of Austrian SMEs in the context of the procurement practice and in this regard examination of the internal Austrian legal framework, a support programme for the tourism and leisure industry; Cross-border support projects for the improvement and expansion of Austria's economic relations with the EU enlargement countries; the structure and policy of regional compensation; the best possible use of the EU Structural Funds; local development in cooperation with the EU using EU programmes; a balanced economic structure with the greatest possible value added in Austria a high-quality economic location based on ecological criteria for people; ensuring high-quality services of general interest, Sustainable continuation of employee participation with access for all employees (profit and/or capital participation). Competition policy Basics: Competition should take place in the interests of the people, consumers, the Austrian small and medium-sized enterprises, the Austrian industry and the employees in these enterprises. The State has a major responsibility for the functioning of the markets. To this end, the Federal Government intends to ensure the following: clear rules and strict control of the market a complete and high-quality control of market power abuse efficient merger control in selected areas according to national economic criteria Equal opportunities and fair competition in Austrian trade in order to ensure quality standards The introduction of a "Master's Business" protected seal as a guide for consumers, the report of an expert commission should be submitted by the end of 2007; proven dual training (praxis plus vocational school) will continue to be the usual training model for the industrial master’s or a career as a professional worker in the future. More competition in the professions Not only from competition policy but also from employment policy considerations, there should be more competition and easier access in the professions. The aim is to increase transparency in the various admission procedures with regard to the services offered, in order to improve career opportunities for graduates and professionals. Regional protection schemes should be reviewed for their needs. Finally, training periods, including necessary practical periods, will be reviewed in the direction of possible streamlining. Court of Justice In particular, the competences of the Bundeskartellanwalt and the BWB are to be merged into the BWB in order to avoid double-tracking. The creation of BWB's first-instance decision-making competence should be examined. Small and medium-sized enterprises The aim is to give small and medium-sized enterprises a secure basis for their economic activity and therefore real equal opportunities for SMEs. Creative economy In order to meet the increasing economic importance of the Austrian creative economy, the Federal Government intends to take the following measures: Forcing cultural education and training; developing political, economic and social conditions to ensure spaces for all forms of art and culture; improving governance structures, i.e. linking cultural, economic and employment policies to develop the social and economic potential of the cultural sector; Building a consistent support tool for creative businesses, in particular strategy plan Creative economy, advice and know-how communication, expansion of innovation promotion, access to external sources of funding, etc.Use custom fonts; Strengthen the know-how transfer for copyright-based recovery strategies. External trade It is important to intervene more politically in the process of globalisation than in the past and to make greater use of opportunities as well as to stop negative developments. Social policy values, such as social compensation, cultural diversity and environmental protection, need to be found more clearly than before in the global economy's rule of law; it is a matter of making globalisation just. The Federal Government aims to further internationalise the Austrian economy, i.e. increase exports of goods, services and foreign direct investment. In view of the importance of the export economy and the need for further internationalisation of the Austrian economy, the Federal Government intends to continue the Internationalisation Plan. The Federal Government is committed to promoting the attractiveness of Austria as an investment location and as a seat of international companies (headquarters policy). Trade in services within the WTO and the GATS As part of its external trade policy, the Federal Government will work towards the following objectives: A continuation of (currently suspended) WTO Doha negotiations is of great importance given the economic importance of further improving market access and multilateral trade rules. The Federal Government will work as far as possible and balancedly as possible in the context of the EU. clear border crossing between commercial and public services: The Federal Government will work at EU level to ensure that public services such as health, education, water management, art and culture (including film) and public transport are not further liberalised in the ongoing GATS negotiations. Parliament will be fully informed and involved on the ongoing negotiations. As far as the public is concerned, maximum transparency is ensured within the framework of EU standards. European Economy Taking advantage of opportunities for the economy in Europe The Federal Government wants to make the best possible use of the opportunities Europe and the European Union offer to the Austrian economy and will therefore take the following measures within the framework of the European Union: developing trans-European networks, promoting new technologies in the field of top-level technology and implementing technologies for SMEs; Priority in the EU budget for economic measures; strengthening SMEs by reducing market entry barriers and improving access to capital markets; Environmental protection and/or environmental protection respectively. sustainable economy as an element of economic and social development. The transitional periods for freedom of movement for workers and freedom to provide services are to be used offensively to prepare the Austrian labour market and the border regions for opening up to Central and Eastern Europe. Research, innovation, technology The challenge is to make a qualitative and quantitative leap forward. The main focus is on achieving the 3% research rate as well as the continuation of structural change: In the next few years, Austria will increasingly become an independent producer of top technology and a top-ranking research location. Austria must develop from the low and medium-sized technology sector to the supplier of high-tech technology. That is why our research and innovation structures for the Oberliga game need to be strengthened. Such a strategy is crucial for growth and employment in Austria. 1. Investing more and more in the long term in research, technology and innovation Austria is to achieve the Lisbon objectives in the FTI area: Based on multi-annual planning, the research rate will be increased to 3% by 2010. These investments are intended to trigger as high private research investment as possible in order to establish the ratio 1/3 publicly financed to 2/3 private R & D quota. For the public sector, this means that the existing budgets and funds of the National Foundation and the currently EUR 295 million from the Offensive Funds (Technology Billions) in 2007 will add 50 million, 100 million in 2008 and 250 million in 2009. and in 2010 by 400 million. Euro will be increased. On this basis, federal expenditure is expected to rise by around 10% per year by 2010. Special attention will be paid to long-term financing security. The Council for Research and Technology Development will continue its advisory role. The separation of strategic and operational tasks must be carried out between ministries and agencies. The very large number of individual funding programmes will be further adjusted by means of portfolio analysis, pooling and priority setting. The results of evaluations are to be taken into account. For the Austrian FTI policy, the European Research Area is an important guide framework. It contributes to its development and tries to benefit from its initiatives, including European research programmes. An efficient and effective tax research funding should be further ensured and further optimised with regard to its impact on smaller companies. 2. Investing means: Building and developing human resources People and their development potential are the largest FTI resource and are particularly supported: Youth promotion, mobility and women are the focus. In the next four years there will be funds for 1000 new jobs for young researchers (postdocs) in the public research system, especially at universities according to budgetary possibilities. The attractiveness of women's research careers and their ability to co-design will be enhanced by institutional and programme-related measures. The objective is a clear increase in the share of women in the public and private sectors. The further development of the structures for the first years as a researcher at the university is crucial for the entire research system: The conversion of doctoral education towards graduate schools is therefore a high priority. Mobility from and to Austria as well as between the sectors should continue to increase in the sense of increasing the attractiveness of the research site Austria. ÖAD as BundesGmbH establish. 3rd. An excellence strategy for the research and innovation location Austria Structural change and technology leadership require excellent public research structures: The universities must be particularly supported in their structural change and in their priority education. With its competitive allocation, the FWF plays a central role in this and is to be further strengthened in the context of the additional funds. This applies to the established promotions and the new clusters of excellence as well as to overhead payments. Cooperation Economics – Science should continue to be publicly supported both directly and through structured initiatives, as well as through the long-term Excellence Programme for Competence Centres (COMET). Institutions and sites with special quality requirements and structural effects on the entire research system are to be developed and expanded: This applies to new initiatives (e.g. ISTA) as well as existing top-level research sites (e.g. Vienna Biocenter). In the institutional context, the reform of the Academy of Sciences is of great importance. 4. Forcing research in the enterprise sector Technology leadership is achieved by companies. This ensures jobs at the Austrian site. They need and receive strong incentives from the public sector: Austria is expected to be consistently attractive as a location for F&E headquarters. With its competitive allocation, the FFG plays a central role and is to be strengthened budgetaryly within the framework of the additional funds. Infrastructure Transport infrastructure and infrastructure projects A modern infrastructure is essential for the success of Austria's economic location. Transport routes – rail, road and Danube – aviation and telecommunications are the life lines of our modern society. They connect people with each other and Austria with the crucial markets for the future. A modern transport policy for people must be based both on the transport needs of the economy and on the social mobility needs of people, as well as on the objectives of environmental protection and the protection of life and health in order to improve the quality of life in Austria as a whole. Due to a meaningful intermodal link between the individual modes of transport, the transport system is optimised. This will ensure the efficient use of the existing Capacity enabled. In order to prevent further shift of modal split at the expense of environmentally compatible modes of transport, it is particularly necessary to force the attraction of rail and waterway. A significant contribution to this can be made to the production of more cost-effectiveness in transport, including external effects. 1.1 Infrastructure planning In order to strengthen the economic location and manage traffic, the infrastructure projects listed in the six-year framework plan of the ÖBB and the ASFINAG construction programme are to be implemented in a timely manner. Prioritisation according to economic criteria: the prioritisation of gaps and the elimination of bottlenecks in the high-level network; in particular, the implementation of those measures in the framework plan, which improve the existing network and are necessary as conditions for operational rationalisation and improvements in the sales sector; The basis of such a plan shall be the functional requirements (performance criteria) on the corridors and axes to be provided with a description of the necessary investments. In order to strengthen the economic location and manage traffic, the infrastructure projects listed in the six-year framework plan of the ÖBB and the ASFINAG construction programme are to be implemented in a timely manner. In order to implement the ÖBB Framework Plan, an investment volume of hr. 6 billion. The investment volume for the construction programme of Asfinag is expected to be 4.5 billion € included. Thus, more than 10 billion euros will be made available for the infrastructure offensive. In addition, the The transfer of the high-level road network to ASFINAG's ownership with the aim of improving capital requirements (IFRS). In the case of road and rail infrastructure, construction costs must be reduced in a massive way. On the basis of European benchmarks, all projects need to be reviewed on the basis of route guidance and development standards. This means that the existing investment plans of Asfinag and ÖBB provide a saving potential of at least 10%. In order to finance the infrastructure offensive, the truck toll is increased by 4 cents and the mineral oil tax on petrol by 1 cent and on diesel by 3 cents. To strengthen the competitiveness of the Austrian transport industry, the car tax for trucks is halved. 1.2 Corridor concept as the basis for infrastructure planning Consideration of the main transport axes in the form of corridors has proved successful. In the context of the development of infrastructure projects, these corridors should be defined in accordance with the requirements of European integration and the regional structure of Austria. For each of these corridors, functional requirements for their performance must be developed. The connection of the individual corridors takes place in the nodes to be defined. In addition to the regional distribution, the intermodal link will also take place, which will enable the overall transport system to be optimised. Against this background, the following points should be added to the individual projects of the ÖBB Framework Plan and the ASFINAG construction programme: Economic efficiency of the project (economic consideration for the infrastructure manager and for each relevant user, incl. Public budgets) The project contributes to the elimination of capacity bottlenecks and/or capacity bottlenecks. Locking gap Transport effect (including interaction between different modes of transport in the corridor) Effects (external effects) Public transport For the agglomeration centres, high quality public transport is an economic survival issue. Cities with poor public transport would collapse economically and ecologically. For rural regions, public transport is an essential prerequisite for mobility. Transport safety Long-term objective must be the so-called “Zero vision”, namely the complete prevention of road fatalities. Measures are as follows: The evaluation and improvement of recently adopted transport safety measures such as ‘primary system’ or ‘light on the day’. Traffic control systems for flexible adjustment of speed limitation according to weather conditions, traffic density, etc. to prevent accidents and accidents. In the sense and with the aim of a uniform vote, the release of speed limits shall be: Motorways and highways according to Immissionsschutzgesetz Luft are federal competence. Increased safety awareness through increased awareness, training and public work, as well as the promotion of modern vehicle safety technologies. In view of the increasing number of accidents in heavy traffic, greater controls are being carried out. In particular, compliance with steering and rest periods, but also weekend driving bans and loading regulations. The aim is to ensure uniform nationally high-quality driving training. The teaching of the professional driver should be adapted in accordance with EU rules in such a way as to ensure equality in the examination of qualifications with the training of the professional driver. Especially high growth will be the East-West transport, while the North-South transit is commuting at a high level. The Federal Government will develop a new strategy for greater cost-reliance in freight transport. In addition, work is being carried out on the construction of an Alpine transit exchange with the Austrian neighbours. Different truck tolls from 2010 The Federal Government ensures that truck toll differentiation does not lead to an erosion of the assessment base at the truck toll. Safe energy. Safe future. For the Austrian Federal Government, ensuring sustainable energy supply in Austria is one of the key challenges of the coming years and decades. In order to increase security of supply with energy and reduce the import of fossil energy, we are increasingly focusing on renewable energy sources, domestic energy production, energy savings, as well as on intensive energy research and new energy technologies. The provision of low-cost energy for consumers and the economy through domestic energy production, security of supply and the promotion of European competition is our goal. Use renewable energies increase in renewable energy in total energy consumption to at least 25% by 2010 and doubling to 45% by 2020 Increase in the share of renewable electricity generation to 80% by 2010, 85% by 2020 Conversion from at least 40 0.000 households to renewable energy sources by 2020, including 100,000 households by 2010 Turnover neutral increase in alternative fuels in the transport sector to 10% by 2010, to 20% by 2020 Master plan for optimal use of hydropower Doubling biomass use by 2010 Non-profit creation of a methane fuel of at least 20 % Biomethane by 2010 Surface-covering network of E85 and Methangas service stations by 2010 Improving the legal framework for biogas supply Save Energy The aim is to strengthen decoupling between economic growth and energy consumption to improve energy intensity. The coordination of a national energy efficiency action programme is carried out by the Austrian Energy Agency. National Energy Efficiency Action Programme Increase energy intensity by at least 5% by 2010, by at least 20% by 2020 Energy check for all Austrian households by 2010 Increasing the recovery rate in residential construction, thus enabling the thermal renovation of all post-war buildings (1950 – 1980) by 2020 In the case of new buildings, the Federal Government, together with the federal states, forces low-energy and passive house standards For 50% of the new building, a climate: active standard is sought From 2015, only more houses and buildings in large-volume housing will be promoted in the area of housing development, which correspond to the “climate active passive house standard” Development and use of energy-efficient devices and solutions (standby) Development of combined heat and power as an efficient process for electricity and heat generation Austrian electricity industry As part of a further consolidation of the electricity industry in Austria, the position of Austrian companies in the European internal electricity market is to be strengthened.At the same time, a focus on renewable energies is to be developed in order to strengthen the international positioning of Austria as a know-how carrier of renewable energy technologies. The gap in the Austrian 380 kV circuit ring is to be reached without delay in order to ensure a reduction of a large-scale power loss risk and the continuous safeguarding of the power supply of companies and households. In the field of grid technology and grid control, increasing decentralised power generation is intended to find new innovative solutions for cost-effective maintenance of grid stability and voltage quality. Energy and climate protection funds In order to achieve the ambitious energy policy objectives and trigger important research and technology impulses, a public law energy and climate protection funds with EUR 500 million, together with the Austrian energy industry, will be created. The objective of the Austrian Energy and Climate Fund is to make a significant contribution in the field of energy research and development to the doubling of renewable energy sources in total energy consumption in Austria by 2020. In concrete terms, the Fund aims to bring new technologies for sustainable energy supply and efficient energy use into economic maturity, to support market penetration of these technologies, and to ensure security of supply through regional resources to increase. The implementation of the objectives of the Energy and Climate Fund should also strengthen the Austrian economic location and Austria's leading role in energy and environmental technology. Reduce energy dependence Austria must increasingly reduce unilateral dependence on energy imports and keep access to as many energy markets open. As a result, competition among producers can be generated and monopoly trends weakened, which can ensure that all citizens and businesses have the most cost-effective and non-discriminatory access to energy. For this purpose, the development of new transport options within the framework of the trans-European networks and the Nabucco gas pipeline as well as the connection to LNG terminals (liquid natural gas) are important elements. Support stabilisation It is precisely because our country remains dependent on energy supplies from political crisis regions that we need to strengthen efforts to stabilise these regions and to strengthen cooperation. Any investment in the political stability of these countries is also an investment in our security of supply. This means, in concrete terms, strengthening the consideration of energy policy concerns in foreign policy. Development of European external energy policy Austria should give impetus to a European external energy policy. Especially when it comes to market access, but also to stability and democracy initiatives, a closed EU policy towards supplier countries and regions can be more effective than single entry of individual countries. Protection of the environment. Take advantage of opportunities. The aim of the Austrian Federal Government is to further develop the sustainable protection of our environment, the secure and sustainable supply of energy and the sustainable promotion of rural areas to preserve the high quality of life of the population and to ensure the livelihoods of our children. The Federal Government is based on the principle that the challenges of modern industrial, educational and service society in the field of environmental and energy policy can only be solved with the methods and innovativeness of this modern society. A modern environmental policy should also strengthen the medium to long-term competitiveness of industry and industry and contribute positively to growth, employment, technology development and technology application. With ambitious but medium-term stable, environmental standards, the innovative power of the economy is to be better used. Active climate protection The objective of Austrian climate policy is to ensure the achievement of the national Kyoto target. For example, the focus lies on: to promote renewable energy and to increase energy efficiency. The updated national climate strategy will be developed quickly by the Federal Government, decided, financed to the extent necessary and fully implemented by all local authorities. A report will be submitted to Parliament each year. Active anti-atomic policy The Austrian Federal Government maintains its conviction that nuclear energy does not constitute a sustainable form of energy supply. Special attention will be paid to the security issue. The creation of high EU safety standards for nuclear installations is also an essential objective of Austrian nuclear policy. Agreed closure obligations of particularly problematic installations must be strictly observed and further closure agreements with EU financial assistance should be sought. Capacity increases of existing installations should not be promoted as much as the construction of new nuclear installations. In all cases of cross-border power plant projects, Austria will continue to take advantage of all possibilities to protect Austrian safety needs under EU law and the ESPOO Convention. Within the framework of the budgetary circumstances, the Austrian early warning system and risk research will be further expanded. At the Temelín nuclear power plant, the zero variant continues to be maintained and the safety dialogue continues intensively. As part of the milking process, the Federal Government is pursuing the objective of implementing the security measures agreed in Annex 1. The Federal Government will continue its efforts to reform the Euratom Treaty. The current Euratom Treaty also contains essential provisions which are important for protecting the population and the environment. The Austrian Federal Government will take general action against the construction of new nuclear power plants at EU level and will take action within the framework of the Community legislation on the strengthening and strengthening of the health safety provisions. The existing system for the treatment and storage of jetting material legally occurring in Austria, e.g. from medical care, X-rays and research must be technically and financially secured in the long term. Administration Management The aim is to introduce administrative benchmarks between the local authorities, in particular the streamlining of the EIA procedures through improved process management among EIA authorities, to strengthen the environmental Senate by attracting supportive members in the chambers, to expand the EIA procedure with its comprehensive procedural and decision-making focus on other areas.
