Children and young people must therefore be at the heart of all future-oriented measures and be optimally encouraged according to their personal abilities, interests and inclinations. Education, science and research make a decisive contribution in the process of transformation from the industrial society to the knowledge society. High-quality education opportunities and the best possible care for children and young people require responsible autonomy at schools, modern structures in school administration, clear rules on learning and performance objectives and a meaningful evaluation culture. This requires best-trained pedagogists. In order to increase opportunities for young people, future-oriented education reforms are needed, which are also aimed at strengthening the motivation, participation and participation of all students, parents and teachers within the framework of the school partnership. We want to further increase the level of education and further increase the quality of education in Austria. The parents' freedom of choice for their children's education must be maintained. In order to further enhance the quality of education in Austria and ensure sustainable, public expenditure on education should be increased overall. Europe and the European Union are to be brought closer to young people. In view of the increasing importance of lifelong learning, networking and permeability between education and training should be further strengthened and the recognition of informally acquired skills increased. Building on the 3-pillar model and the 2003 and 2004 pension reforms, adjustments are being made in the following areas. This is done in accordance with the important principle that the loads between older and young generations must be fairly distributed. Only in this way can the generation contract continue to be maintained. Pension calculation A working group consisting of social partners, government representatives and other experts will consider the provisions currently in force on pension schemes or pension schemes. -to carry out an evaluation and to make proposals for amendments with a view to improving transparency and simplification. This provided that no substantial intervention into existing pension law (both contribution and benefit rights) is made. Retirement An extension of the discount-free pension scheme by 55/60 under the long-term insurance scheme by 2010 (so-called ‘hackler scheme’) is intended to improve transitional law for those groups of persons who have made long contributions to the scheme. Furthermore, the aim is not to make any reductions in the outflow rule for this group by the year 2010. The current ‘double deductions’ in the case of the use of a corridor pension in transitional law are not in the current form of actuarial principles. It is therefore intended to be mitigated (in the result half of the discount in the old law). Heavy-worker's pension It is examined whether the life expectancy of some heavy workers groups is significantly lower than that of other workers. In the case of evidence of a significant difference, heavy-worker pensions should be redesigned in such a way as to allow for a reduction-free pension if life expectancy is involved. Child training periods (for pension account) The consideration of child rearing periods is to be changed in such a way as to take the current additive crediting of the credits on the pension account from a value-secured contribution basis (start-up value 1.350.- €). Invalidity pensions A working group consisting of social partners, government representatives and other experts is expected to draw up proposals for a reorganisation of invalidity pension law by 1.1.2008. Several occupational groups are treated differently when granting pensions for reduced employment (in turn invalidity pensions). Harmonization should also be sought in this area. For older people who are disadvantaged because of their reduced employment in the labour market but who do not yet meet the requirements for a disability pension, it is necessary to consider whether an improvement can be achieved. Sustainability factor The negotiators agree that the existing sustainability factor will be amended towards an automatic pension scheme with effect from 2010. Changes in life expectancy automatically lead to activation of the sustainability factor. Harmonization The negotiators agree that in the next legislative period, it is intended to influence the federal states and municipalities to promote the harmonisation of the different pension systems. The aim is to create a uniform pension right for all pensioners based on the Federal Pension Act (General Pension Act and Additional Schemes). Combating poverty Further reforms in the Austrian social security system are necessary for many reasons. The extension of life expectancy and the reduction of the number of children, the increase in so-called "precious" employment conditions, the increased competitive pressure on all markets, the increased integration of Austria into the world economy and membership in the EU lead to new challenges. One of the challenges, however, is the poverty that exists in Austria. In a rich country such as Austria, the substantial reduction of poverty – provided for the corresponding political will – represents a soluble task. The aim is to further strengthen the fight against poverty in order to reduce the number of people at risk of poverty and the acutely poor. The instrument for this should be the introduction of a needs-oriented minimum guarantee. This is accompanied by a minimum wage (on the basis of a general collective contract) of EUR 1,000.-. The amount of the minimum guarantee in 2007 is Euro 726,- gross (14 times). The introduction of demand-oriented minimum security takes place in several steps. The first step was to increase the compensatory allowance rate to Euro 726,- in 2007. An agreement will then be reached between the Federal Government and the countries for a minimum social security scheme for the harmonization and fixation of the state's social assistance to the level of € 726,- (possibly in stages). There is a need for separate negotiations with the countries. In order to increase the transparency of social services data, it is necessary that the Federal Government and countries significantly improve their data exchange. The compensatory allowance rate shall be the reference value of the risk to poverty in Austria. Subject to the implementation of a requirement-oriented minimum guarantee in the federal states, the development of minimum-security elements in unemployment insurance law is carried out at the same time: The 60 % net replacement rate system for single persons under the compensatory allowance rate is fully represented in the emergency aid, i.e. emergency aid is assessed at 95% of the net replacement rate raised to up to 60%. In the case of persons with family supplements, the net replacement rate increased to up to 80% will also be used as a basis for calculating the emergency aid. The accounting rules on partner income in the event of emergency aid are amended in such a way as not to lead to a household income under the family allowance rate (including child supplements). The requirement for the award of the service is at least the willingness to work in all those who are able to work. The rules on visibility are made fairer and more practical. Long-term unemployed are involved in non-profit labour projects and are committed to continuing training. This ensures that the need-oriented minimum guarantee is not an unemployed basic income. The AMS will provide support for the workable social assistance providers for reintegration into the labour market with the aim of achieving a one-stop shop with a view to disbursing the services from the need-oriented minimum guarantee. The needs and assets audit shall be carried out by the social assistance bodies. Central Element of the need test is also the use of one's own assets - for: If you own assets, you must use them before you have the right to aid from the general public. There is an appropriate exploitation of assets for social assistance workers, where the (self-inhabited) residence is assessed with a fictitious rent and a car necessary for professional training is not used. Maintenance entitlements shall be based on those values which normally flow to the dependant after actions and executions. “Social tourism” is avoided by appropriate link to the right to permanent residence. Health The Federal Government is committed to comprehensive medical care for all people regardless of age and income. The aim is a long life expectancy in good health, maximum patient satisfaction and comprehensive protection against the financial risk of a disease. The principle of solidarity, equal and low-quality access to services and high quality and efficiency in the provision of services shall apply. In order to ensure access to medical progress for all groups of the population, it is necessary for all decision-makers to take a particularly careful approach to existing resources. The focus of the Federal Government's health policy is on patients' needs. Gender-medicine is taken into account as a continuous principle at all levels of health care. 1. Prevention, health promotion and public health An extended prevention and health promotion at the content, structural and financial level is intended to reach people in their living environments, such as work, kindergarten, school or community. The following measures are therefore adopted: A Health Promotion Act as 4. Pillar prevention and health promotion; based on agreed targets in relation to civil disease, the promotion of healthy living environment and lifestyles (movement, nutrition, addiction and risk of accident). (ii) the creation of a network of national and regional authorities and the creation of local centres of competence; (iii) the setting-up of local and regional authorities; and (iii) the creation of local and regional centres of competence; (iii) the creation of local and regional authorities; and (iii) the creation of regional and local authorities; and (iii) the Use of existing structures (e.g. Hospitals, municipalities and social insurance). Extensive funding for prevention and health promotion is reviewed in accordance with the respective competence. Epidemiologically sound prevention and health reporting, research and evaluation. Anchoring a legally extended non-smoking in-house protection (especially through strict regulations also in locals through spatially separated smoking zones). National addiction and alcohol strategy, especially for young people. Further development of public health services and novelties of the Epidemic Act and clear rules in disaster prevention. Targeted use of vaccination programs (especially in children and against epidemic diseases). Development of systematic screening programs (brass cancer, colon cancer and prostate). 2. Development of integrated supply Based on the patient's needs, health processes must be designed in such a way as to ensure that prevention, diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation and care are provided in the right order, from the right place, in appropriate time and with guaranteed quality and maximum results. In principle: Integrated care is agreed as a health policy target for the cooperation partners Federal Government, countries, social security and all service providers. The overall planning of a patient-oriented service offer covers all supply areas. Quality and cost-effectiveness of the individual sectors are based on the effectiveness and efficiency of the overall system. The funding follows the principle of ‘money follows performance’. Upgrade of the role of general physicians and other health professionals. Internal security Joint findings It is a central task of the state to protect the freedom and security of its citizens. Freedom is certainly not imaginable. The Austrians have a right to be protected from crime. Internal security Austria is one of the safest countries in the world. The Executive has implemented necessary structural measures. On-going evaluation is required in order to address future developments. The current organisational structure and the current system of federal police at federal, national and district level will continue to apply in their principles. For the police, it is necessary that their lives be regulated from education to career planning with a fair salary. Consideration should be given to the specific psychological and physical loads and the needs of professional protection in the field of executives. The staff level shall be adapted to the needs in a human resources development plan with a view to future retirements and the forthcoming Schengen extension and shall be determined over the legislative period. If necessary, an increase in the staffing level shall be assumed. In the next few years, the Schengen extension to our neighbouring countries is imminent. The transfer of the officials currently employed in the border service to a new system requires compensation measures such as the veiling and construction of priority services in the border area and on major transport routes that need to be developed rapidly. Where necessary, local job changes shall be carried out in a socially balanced manner for the staff concerned. Because of the enormous appeal of young women to the police profession and the growing proportion of women in the police service (dz. Approximately 10 %), new challenges arise in the field of personnel management. Criminal law and criminal law All necessary steps will be taken to ensure the entry into force of the criminal process reform by 1.1.2008. Hiefor this, it will be necessary to promote the permissiveness between judges and prosecutors, to ensure constitutional and parliamentary control of the prosecution monopoly of the public prosecutors as the body of the judicial system, to speedily advance the reform of the main and judicial proceedings and to prepare organisational measures for the smooth change of systems. In this context, an adequate indictment infrastructure will also be ensured by the District Courts. Cooperation with the judicial and police authorities of the countries of origin of foreign criminals is aimed at preventing “criminal tourism” to improve and intensify. The aim is to strengthen significantly the efforts of the home country to take over the penalty, in particular from the point of view that successful resocialisation in the social environment of the home country is much more likely than in Austria. It is particularly important to strengthen the fight against trafficking in human beings and the sexual exploitation of women. In the field of substantive criminal law, sanctions should be extended, in particular through the introduction of non-profit services, as a penalty in combination with other forms of sanctions, and the possibility of a conditional redundancie while strengthening the prevention of relapse for residents, in particular by facilitating the provision of conditions. In the case of non-residence persons, rules are to be found to relieve the execution of such persons in accordance with fundamental and equality law. In appropriate cases and if penalties are not possible in the home Member State, the early release of third-country nationals is to be linked to an expulsion and an effective residence or residence. and the prohibition of return. The decision-making system should be optimised in order to ensure individual case-by-case justice in the event of conditional redundancies. Ensuring a functioning judicial system for young people is urgently needed, in particular in order to re-integrate once more troubled young people into society and reduce crime for the future. Resocialisation barriers should also be avoided and additional effective measures should be taken against all forms of violence in the family, in particular violence against women and children. In order to improve the possibility of abduction of long-term liberty and violence, a new law on penalties should be created similar to that of §§ 39 and 313 StGB, which allows for an increase in the basic penalty to the one and a half times if the circumstances of a threat of liberty or violence or the threat of a victim are particularly serious, especially if the exercise of violence goes on for a longer period of time and if the circumstances of liberation or violence are particularly painful and equal to a martyrdom. In order to avoid the execution of replacement sentences, the legislative steps to avoid imprisonment by non-profit work are to be taken on the basis of the results of the ongoing pilot project. In order to improve the basis for decision-making on criminal law policy, a general and specific set-aside statistics should be created. A research project will also improve the basis for assessing the risk of perpetrators. In addition, the establishment of an anonymous recruitment statistics by the public prosecutors is required. The case-law should not be abolished, but merely reformed (in particular, better selection and training of the parties, the public with respect to the law, the written obligation to state reasons). In the area of criminal enforcement, the organisation reform of the judicial system should continue and quality assurance should be introduced to ensure efficiency. That one. In view of the modified sentence structure, legislative measures are intended to provide for the conditions for improved differentiation between dangerous criminal offenders and those accessible to resocialisation; in this sense, there will be a differentiation between resident-strengthened offenders and others. In the course of these reforms, the training and training programme should also be improved in the judicial institutions. Media and telecommunications The aim of the Federal Government's media policy is to ensure a pluralistic media landscape with qualitative offers. It is about securing the competitiveness of Austria as a media and cultural location, expanding the dual broadcasting system and implementing European standards. In this together. It is important to address the challenges posed by digitization and technological developments. Print media, radio, Internet and online media as well as the offer via telephone services, whether mobile or via the fixed network, grow together. Independent regulator Media and telecommunications questions The Kommunestria Media Authority and the RTR business unit must be developed into a constitutionally independent, converging media and telecommunications authority. The instance and procedure will take place in two stages and bring legal certainty to media providers as quickly as possible. In the interests of equality of competition, all regulatory authorisations shall be issued by the regulator to all electronic providers. Private broadcasting A dual broadcasting system, with an unmistakable public-law broadcasting system on the one hand and independent, competitive private broadcasters on the other, is an essential part of a living democracy. Finance Budgetary policy The objective of budgetary policy is a balanced budget over the economic cycle; the Federal Government is committed to a sustainable budgetary and financial policy, which responds to economic weaknesses in an appropriate way and balances over an economic cycle. The Federal Government pays attention to the common budgetary responsibility of all local authorities within the meaning of the Austrian Stability Pact. The objective of the budget balanced over the economic cycle requires discipline not only on the expenditure side but also on the income of taxes and taxes. Spaces for tax relief are being developed and must be manageable in the light of the fact that important future investment for growth and employment, the location of Austria, social security or other important public tasks must also be carried out. In its budgetary policy, the Federal Government pursues in particular the following objectives: Full employment (especially prevention of all types of youth unemployment) Modernising the economic location through technological, economic and social innovation Supporting the economic location and strengthening its competitiveness a budget balanced over the economic cycle Sustainable financing of social security Manufacture of equal opportunities between sexes Increased efficiency in public administration Increased emphasis on forward-looking budgets With the exception of the additional expenditure agreed in the government programme, all other projects and projects of the Federal Government are subject to a reservation of funding (see Annex "Middle-term growth and budget path"). In order to pay the price, all fees will be charged, e.g. Vignette undergoes annual valorization. In all investments and procurements as well as in running operations, the budgetary principles of economic efficiency, economy, efficiency and cost-effectiveness must apply at each stage. The Federal Government will also work at European level to ensure that financial and budgetary policies make an active contribution to growth and employment in the European Union. The Austrian Federal Government sets the following priorities: Growth and employment, research and development, infrastructure expansion, education, poverty prevention and social security, environmental protection and sustainability. Tax reform In this legislative period, the Federal Government will implement a major tax reform with a tangible discharge of taxpayers and the economy without counter-financing. This supports a positive economic development in Austria. In order to further improve the service provided to taxpayers, the financial management should send pre-filled tax returns to the taxable person.
